A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from GenCL to GenOL. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original continual-learning and joint-training experiments, multimodal reasoning results, component ablations, and generated-image analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, bias measurements, sensitivity studies, and experiments with alternative models and real examples.

M1.justification: The default HIRPG and CONAN procedures, generator ensemble, and replay framework are retained. v4 Section A.26 adds HIRPG-FT, which adapts SDXL using LoRA and real examples, omitting CONAN for a single-generator comparison. This is a limited method extension.

E1.justification: v4 adds ImageNet/ImageNet-R evaluation, Birds-31 fine-grained domain generalization, and a generation scenario supplied with real reference examples. PACS, DomainNet, CIFAR-10-W, both Bongard benchmarks, and joint training already appeared in v3; their relocation or increased prominence is not new coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds Real-Fake, IE, Seafaring, and Tiara to the CIL comparison, and the latter three to MVCIL. Table 4 adds AL and LDM-S to selection comparisons; Section A.19 adds HCL and H-SCL; Figure 17 adds DreamCache, DreamBooth, and Bootpig. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate alternative learners (MISA and C-Prompt), LLMs (LLaMA3-8B and Qwen3-8B), bias, and generation using 1, 3, 5, or 10 real examples. Recognizability also changes from an ImageNet-pretrained ViT with linear probing in v3 A.16 to a ViT trained from scratch on MA data in v4 A.13. The PDFs do not establish that the retained recognizability scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: v4 adds demographic and geographical bias analyses, downstream bias evaluation, tree-depth/width and temperature/truncation sensitivity, learner and LLM robustness checks, real-example sensitivity, inter-branch prompt similarity, and concrete generation failures. Original component ablations, RMD-selection analyses, and scaling plots remain, often relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds/task splits and report means with SEM. v4 A.2 introduces an explicit exception for ImageNet-R because of computational constraints; its Table 1 provides no uncertainty estimates or alternative run count. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Most matched original CIL and MVCIL scores are unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results for new comparators, benchmarks, and analyses. Birds-31, for example, reports lower GenOL AUC than MA but higher final accuracy. There is also an unexplained numerical revision: CLIP-ZS's CIFAR-10-W joint-training score changes from 57.14 in v3 Table 9 to 14.69 in v4 Table 25, while v4 Table 26 retains 57.14.

T1.justification: The prompt recurrences, RMD formulation, selection probabilities, metric formulas, and incremental mean/covariance derivations are substantively retained. Changes to notation and equation presentation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly restricts new concepts to relative novelty for deployed systems and foregrounds applicability to online learning without distribution shifts. The central HIRPG/CONAN contributions and performance claims remain. Joint training already supported the broader application in v3, so this is chiefly a refinement of contribution scope.

C2.justification: v3's brief limitations emphasize absent learner feedback and generator quality. v4 Section 7 substantially expands discussion of scalability, memorization/privacy, and concepts outside generator knowledge. New analyses interpret bias reduction, the ID/OOD tradeoff from real-example fine-tuning, and generation failures, including an argument that imperfect images can improve robustness.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the generated-data link and future code-release promise with a stated code repository, and discloses exclusion of person-related released images. It adds ImageNet training/memory settings, bias attribution prompts, DomainNet hyperparameter-selection information, explicit template reuse, and computational/storage comparisons. These materially expand reproducibility information, although some settings conflict internally.

R1.justification: v4 substantially broadens positioning around active learning, hard-negative selection, few-shot generator adaptation, bias/privacy, and relative novelty. Newly cited works include Park et al. (2022), Robinson et al. (2021), Ruiz et al. (2023), Mandal et al. (2023), and Cossu and Shaheen et al. (2022). Much of the original continual-learning review is retained in A.15.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and reorganized. GenCL becomes GenOL; related-work material moves into the appendix, while limitations and qualitative analysis gain main-text sections. Author affiliations, publication headers, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v4 adopts new journal typesetting, reformats Figure 1, expands comparison tables, and relocates many existing displays. It adds bias charts, sensitivity plots, a prompt-similarity heatmap, and a failure-image panel. The earlier Horse prompt-example table is removed, while the other three prompt-example tables remain.

improvement.justification: Broader comparator and model-dependence tests strengthen empirical support, while Section 7 and A.36 provide clearer applicability boundaries and concrete failures than v3's brief limitations. These gains are tempered by new reporting problems: Table 7's ImageNet-R class counts are inconsistent, A.23 contradicts A.4 on tree depth, and Table 25 introduces unexplained CLIP-ZS values. The changed recognizability protocol with unchanged scores further limits confidence. Overall, the validation and transparency improve, but the net gain is limited.
